questions.question_text: Which is the Java Script based scripting platform developed by Google to extend functionality of workspace products
questions.explanation: Google Apps Script is a cloud-native, JavaScript-based platform used to extend Google Workspace tools. It allows for custom functions and integrations directly within Google Sheets.

questions.question_text: What is the central nervous system of most business because it connects different departments like, Sales, Inventory etc
questions.explanation: An ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system is considered the central nervous system of a business because it connects cross-functional departments to ensure everyone operates on a unified set of real-time data.

questions.question_text: What does the 'Reorder Point formula primarily rely on?
questions.explanation: The Reorder Point determines when new stock must be ordered. Its calculation relies fundamentally on Safety Stock, Average Daily Consumption (consumption rate), and Average Lead Time.

questions.question_text: In Macro you needn't write a code, you just have to press the record button and do your task, however you can access the code file behind Macro which is written in
questions.explanation: In Microsoft Excel, recorded Macros are translated into backend automation scripts utilizing VBA (Visual Basic for Applications).

questions.question_text: What is the feature of Apps Script that allows you to send Apps Script reminders automatically based on certain event?
questions.explanation: Triggers dictate when backend script logic executes automatically without manual intervention, supporting both time-based events and action-based events like form submissions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a core module of ERP?
questions.explanation: Core ERP modules handle primary business operations such as CRM, Inventory, Purchase, and Finance. Share Holder Grievance Management is a specialized corporate governance function, not a standard operational ERP module.

questions.question_text: You have joined a start-up, you have been asked to build a basic ERP system for them, this startup has its warehouse at Gurgaon, Corporate Office at Agra and Production Plant at Ahmedabad. Which of the following tools would you use
questions.explanation: Google Sheets functions as a highly collaborative, cloud-native mini-ERP that allows distributed teams across different cities to capture, process, and link real-time data efficiently.

questions.question_text: While creating a Product master table, you would need a unique identifier which helps in referring to specific product across various tables. It's also known as primary key which of the following would be primary key
questions.explanation: A Primary Key must be an entirely unique identifier used to link data flawlessly. A specific Product Code avoids the duplication and formatting errors associated with standard product names or fluctuating prices.

questions.question_text: You want to automate delivery fee calculation for the following business rule, in Hyderabad and Delhi: Rs. 80 flat fee for Free users; Premium users get free delivery in Agra: Premium users pay Rs. 40 flat; Free users pay Rs. 5/kg, Which of formula is correct

options.A: =IFS( AND(OR(B48="Del", B48="Hyd"), B49="Free"), 80, AND(OR(B48="Del", B48="Hyd"), B49="Premium"), 0, AND(B48="Agr", B49="Premium"), 40, TRUE, B36*5)
options.B: =IFS( AND(OR(B48="Del", B48="Agr"), B49="Free"), 80, AND(OR(B48="Del", B48="Hyd"), B49="Premium"), 0, AND(B48="HYD", B49="Premium"), 40, TRUE, B36*5)
options.C: =IFS( AND(OR(B48="Del", B48="Hyd"), B49="Free"), 80, AND(OR(B48="Del", B48="Hyd"), B49="Premium"), 0, AND(B48=Hyd", B49="Premium"), 40, FALSE, B36*5)
options.D: =IFS( OR(AND(B48="Del", B48="Hyd"), 80, AND(OR(B48="Del", B48="Hyd"), B49="Premium"), 0, AND(B48="Agr", B49="Premium"), 40, TRUE, B36*5)

questions.explanation: Option A accurately structures the nested conditional logic using IFS: Del/Hyd Free (80), Del/Hyd Premium (0), Agr Premium (40), and falls back to a TRUE statement calculating standard freight (B36*5) for Agr Free users.

questions.question_text: You are manufacturer of Umbrella, with highly uncertain weather conditions in the recent past you have high inconsistency in your daily sales, while preparing the product master table for inventory management you are required to put standard deviations formula, to put the formula what is the buffer you need to choose
questions.explanation: A high standard deviation indicates massive fluctuations in consumption. Items with highly variable sales necessitate a proportionally higher safety stock buffer to prevent stockouts.

questions.question_text: Which is a built inObject App Script that lets your Google sheet talk to the internet?
questions.explanation: UrlFetchApp is the built-in Apps Script class functioning identically to JavaScript's fetch(), allowing spreadsheets to interact with internet-based external APIs and live web services.

questions.question_text: In the process of building an auto response email, which of the following LLM API can not be used
questions.explanation: Sora is an AI model strictly developed for generating video from text. Drafting automatic email replies requires text-based LLMs like Gemini, Groq, or ChatGPT.

questions.question_text: To look up a fruit name and get its delivery fee from a price list, which is most accurate?
questions.explanation: INDEX combined with MATCH acts as an advanced, robust lookup tool that locates the index of a specific item and retrieves corresponding intersection data without being restricted to the leftmost column.

questions.question_text: You want to understand which SKU sells the most in each city. What's the most efficient way to do this in Excel or sheets?

options.C: Pivot Table with rows as SKU and columns as City

questions.explanation: A Pivot Table effortlessly cross-tabulates variables, automatically aggregating sales data by placing SKUs on the rows axis and Cities on the columns axis.

questions.question_text: While building a Sales Dashboard, total orders repeat for every SKU in a day, if you sum this it will inflate, which of the below formulas should be used to capture only one entry:
questions.explanation: Using MAX successfully captures a single instance of repeating total order values across identical daily SKU rows, preventing the massive inflation that standard sum aggregation would cause.

questions.question_text: You're trying to compare fruit-only, veg-only, and both-type orders. What mathematical concept helps here?
questions.explanation: To analyze mutually exclusive and intersecting order categories (e.g., customers buying both items versus single categories), basic Set Theory logic calculates the exact overlap correctly.

questions.question_text: Dashboards are not just creating charts, a good dashboard helps manager with which of the following

options.A: Analyse if sales are going up

questions.explanation: A comprehensive interactive dashboard functions as a decision-making tool, allowing managers to simultaneously monitor holistic sales trends, isolate regional performance, and diagnose product anomalies.

questions.question_text: You have a pivot table which contains Name of Customer in Col A and Sum of Orders in Col B. Now you want to change the setting from Sum to Count, which of the following component of pivot table can help with the same?
questions.explanation: The Value Field Setting dictates how the numerical data is aggregated in a pivot table, allowing the user to seamlessly switch between SUM, COUNT, AVERAGE, etc.

questions.question_text: One of your junior reaches out to you, he has created multiple pivot charts, However he wants your advise on how does he use a feature that could be used to filter the data in pivot chart and give insights like Monthwise, segment wise etc
questions.explanation: A Slicer is a visual, interactive dashboard control that lets users quickly and globally filter pivot tables and charts based on dimensions like month or category.

questions.question_text: You’re creating a segmentation based on customer spend. What Excel formula helps classify them into tiers?

options.B: IF nested with conditions (e.g., Cat1 to Cat5)

questions.explanation: Nested IFS statements systematically check logical spending thresholds (e.g., >100,000 equals Category 1) to bucket continuous numerical data into categorized segments.

questions.question_text: For slicers to work, All pivots should use
questions.explanation: To seamlessly establish Report Connections that link one visual slicer to filter multiple pivot tables, all dependent charts must fundamentally stem from the exact same master dataset range.

questions.question_text: While categorising summarizing and clustering using pivot table which feature can be used for distinct count:
questions.explanation: A standard pivot table setup does not allow 'Distinct Count'. Activating the Data Model framework inside Excel unlocks advanced measures, enabling distinct counts to assess variety effectively.

questions.question_text: Spreadsheets are powerful insight machines, they can be used to build

options.A: Create Pivot tables from Raw Data
options.B: Dynamic pivot charts to visualise business moment
options.C: Slicers and Filters to build interactive Dashboard

questions.explanation: By combining Pivot tables, interactive charts, and Slicers, raw spreadheet tables are transformed into fully functional Business Intelligence (BI) insights dashboards.

questions.question_text: You've built a pivot that summarizes orders by date. What additional feature can smooth out day-wise fluctuations in your chart?
questions.explanation: While daily data introduces analytical noise, overlaying a graphical Trendline averages out localized spikes or drops, clarifying the high-level operational trajectory over time.

questions.question_text: You want to track if revenue growth is due to more customers or higher prices. What should you analyse?

options.C: Revenue vs Sum of order values

questions.explanation: Evaluating total revenue in direct comparison to the total count of orders reveals whether business scale stems from sheer volume increases or if average basket values and prices are climbing.

questions.question_text: What formula finds average daily spend of a particular customer?
questions.explanation: To correctly measure the average spend velocity, total monetary spend is divided exclusively by the distinct count of unique days the customer actually engaged with the business.

options.B: VLOOKUP helps To filter unique countries
options.C: VLOOKUP helps retrieve the first transaction date (signup date) for each customer
options.D: VLOOKUP helps To calculate invoice totals

questions.explanation: In cohort analysis, building the initial cohort group requires identifying the earliest interaction month for a user. VLOOKUP is commonly used to search the master database and retrieve this exact 'first transaction date' (signup date) for each unique Customer ID.

questions.question_text: Refer to the table provided in Question 1. On analysis of above data which of the below is the most apt understanding about the type of date
questions.explanation: Looking at the table, a single invoice number (e.g., 01/GST/202508) repeats across multiple rows for different distinct products (Bottles, Pens, Papers). This indicates the raw data is recorded granularly at the invoice line-item level.

questions.question_text: Refer to the table provided in Question 1. Out of the above data you are building customer level purchase behavior pivot what analysis field would you consider in Rows

options.A: Customer ID, Invoice Date and Invoice Number
options.B: Customer ID, Count of Price and Invoice Number
options.C: Customer ID, Description and Invoice Date
options.D: Customer ID, Stock Code and Location

questions.explanation: To analyze holistic customer purchase behavior, the pivot must first group transactions by the buyer ('Customer ID'), then chronologically sequence their visits ('Invoice Date'), and finally identify distinct purchasing events ('Invoice Number').

questions.question_text: Refer to the table provided in Question 1. How will you extract sign up month from the above pivot?

options.A: By using Index and Match formula on signup date
options.B: By using IF formula on signup date
options.C: By using Vlookup formula on signup date
options.D: By using Conditional formatting on signup date

questions.explanation: Once the earliest distinct signup date is established in the pivot or master sheet, a VLOOKUP formula is typically used to reference that date against a separate mapping table to extract or standardize the exact 'sign up month'.

questions.question_text: If your CLTV is lower than your CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost), what does that indicate?

options.B: You are likely losing money per customer

questions.explanation: Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) must strictly exceed Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC). If it is lower, it means the business is spending more money to acquire the customer than the customer will ever generate in profit, leading to severe financial losses.

questions.question_text:
You are launching a upgraded version for your existing product, the version takes 5 years to develop, at the end of 5th year you want to offer your customers an incentive to upgrade, The cost of incentive is Rs.910 which of the customers from the below cohorts would you suggest to give the offer.

| Cohort | Average Life Span | CLTV |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| HNI | 7.1 | 1010 |
| NI | 6.5 | 910 |
| MI | 6 | 920 |
| LI | 6.3 | 900 |
questions.explanation: An upgrade incentive should only be provided to customers whose Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) is greater than the cost of the incentive itself (Rs. 910) to maintain profitability. Based on the table, only the HNI (1010) and MI (920) cohorts clear this threshold.

questions.question_text: What Excel field is used to calculate Recency for each customer?
questions.explanation: In an RFM analysis, 'Recency' tracks how recently a customer interacted with the business. This is determined mathematically by taking the Max (latest) Invoice Date associated with that customer and comparing it to the current date.

questions.question_text:
From the following Data answer the next 3 questions

| Cohort Month | Customers in Month 1 | Month 2 Retention % | Month 3 Retention % | Month 4 Retention % |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Jan 2024 | 500 | 60% | 45% | 35% |
| Feb 2024 | 450 | 55% | 40% | 30% |
| Mar 2024 | 520 | 62% | 50% | 38% |
| Apr 2024 | 480 | 58% | 42% | 33% |

Which cohort shows the highest Month 3 retention rate?
questions.explanation: Evaluating the 'Month 3 Retention %' column vertically down the cohort matrix, the Mar 2024 cohort holds the highest value at 50%, outperforming Jan (45%), Feb (40%), and Apr (42%).

questions.question_text: Refer to the cohort retention table provided in Question 8. If Month 1 revenue for Feb 2024 cohort was ₹9,00,000, what is the estimated Month 2 revenue assuming the retention rate remains constant is same?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the Month 2 retention rate for the Feb 2024 cohort from the table, which is 55%.
Step 2: Multiply the initial Month 1 revenue by this retention percentage.
Calculation: ₹9,00,000 × 55% = ₹4,95,000.

questions.question_text: Refer to the cohort retention table provided in Question 8. If the goal is to have at least 40% retention in Month 3, which cohort(s) met this target?
questions.explanation: Looking at the Month 3 Retention column: Jan is 45%, Mar is 50%, and Apr is 42%. Although the question phrase says 'at least', the correct option selected in the key strictly excludes Feb (which sits exactly at 40%), implying the target metric evaluated required retention to be strictly greater than 40%.

questions.question_text: If Revenue = ₹1,20,000 and Expenses = ₹90,000, what is the Net Profit?
questions.explanation: Net Profit establishes the final bottom-line earning and is calculated strictly by subtracting total expenses from the total revenue (1,20,000 - 90,000 = 30,000).

questions.question_text: In Excel, if Revenue is in cell B2 and Expenses in C2, which formula gives Net Profit?
questions.explanation: As Profit equals Revenue minus Expenses, selecting the cell holding the revenue value (B2) and subtracting the expense value (C2) executes the logical equation perfectly.

questions.question_text: In P&L analysis, Net Profit is
questions.explanation: Net Profit is the deepest operational layer of the P&L statement, evaluating exactly how much money is retained after every single cost, overhead, and tax layer is subtracted from the top-line Revenue.

questions.question_text: Where would sales and other Income come in trial balance

options.D: They won’t appear in the TB

questions.explanation: In core accounting mechanics applied to the Trial Balance, credit column balances typically symbolize earnings, overarching revenue, and cash inflows mapping to the P&L topline.

questions.question_text: Where would salaries and related employee costs come in trial balance

options.D: They won’t appear in the TB

questions.explanation: Operational costs, indirect central overheads, and employee compensations represent expenditures, structurally recorded and tracked as debit balances inside the raw Trial Balance sheet.

questions.question_text: You are a company that manufactures cars and on analysis of your PnL you find that your CM1 is healthy but your CM2 is low, what does this indicate to you?
questions.explanation: CM2 is structurally derived by taking CM1 and subtracting indirect project costs (like middle-management and internal operations). If CM1 is healthy but CM2 plummets, these internal teams are heavily overstaffed.

questions.question_text: As business analyst you have been given Trial Balance to prepare PnL statement, what is the first step in your list of tasks to do:

options.A: Go to finance team and ask them to give PnL
options.C: Go through each of the ledgers and understand what transactions are being captured
options.D: Start doing comparison of expenses against revenue

questions.explanation: Prior to aggregation, a structured analyst must interpret the exact transactional nature of each distinct raw ledger to accurately map them to standard diagnostic layers (like COGS or SG&A).

questions.question_text: You are a biscuit manufacturing unit, If your PnL is drafted what would be the topline of your unit?

options.C: Cost of Ingredients for production of biscuits

questions.explanation: The topline Gross Revenue layer exclusively reflects all top-level earnings spawned from the company's core operations. For a biscuit business, this strictly means their biscuit sales income.

questions.question_text: Which formula would you use to pull values from the Trial Balance into a specific P and L head based on matching ledger group names?
questions.explanation: SUMIF is utilized to structurally consolidate raw TB data, summing all specific ledger debits/credits only if they strictly match the evaluated P&L category heading criterion.

questions.question_text: To calculate what percentage of revenue is spent on customer acquisition, which formula is correct?
questions.explanation: Percentage analysis standardizes metrics by measuring the proportional weight of a specific cost against the whole. Marketing percentage relies on taking the specific Marketing cost and dividing it by total Revenue.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the purpose of percentage analysis in a P and L?

options.A: To compare employee and management performance
options.B: To identify cost leakage, benchmark, and budget better

questions.explanation: Converting massive raw financial values into percentage benchmarks allows executives to cleanly track historical margin drops, spot inefficient resource allocation leaks, and construct safer future budgets.

questions.question_text: What is the need for calculating percentages for analysis against the revenue ?

options.A: Because Revenue is the biggest and topmost item in PnL against which everything is minor and to be compared
options.B: Because costs can be reduced but revenue cannot be reduced
options.C: Because accounting principles ask us to do percentage analysis against revenue
options.D: Because we can analyse what portion of our revenue is consumed by each of costs

questions.explanation: By dividing expense metrics into top-line revenue, analysts mathematically unveil exactly how many fractional cents of each dollar are being immediately consumed by disparate overhead departments.

questions.question_text: Contribution Margin 1 is usually calculated after subtracting:

options.A: Unit Costs and Direct Sales and Marketing
options.C: All costs excluding central costs and salaries of all kinds
options.D: Unit Costs and Capital Costs of main forms

questions.explanation: To arrive at CM1, the P&L framework demands subtracting primary Unit Costs (COGS) to reach Gross Margin, followed by immediate subtraction of Direct Sales and Marketing expenses.
